name: Brooklyn printing-plant air conditioning
description: A plant air-conditioning system controlled humidity and temperature for industrial printing.

places.note: Modern country or regional reference; historic political boundaries are not implied.

date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: A printing plant in Brooklyn used a system designed by Willis Carrier to control conditions affecting multicolor printing.
events.caveats: The corporate retrospective is associated with the inventor; the initial system used well water and compressor cooling was added in 1903.

evidence.supports: Carrier’s history dates installation and describes the humidity problem.
History credits the design to Carrier.

contributions.resource: Used the system in a printing plant

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest event sourced for this particular record; not a claim of global origin.

caveats: Earlier refrigeration and climate-control practices exist; this plant is one industrial use.

measures.conditions: Manufacturer retrospective describes a target; not an independently measured year-round performance.

evidence.supports: The company reports a target of 55% relative humidity.
